title: Losing work
hook: unemployment met with chardi kala and help from the sangat
tomorrow: Chacha's last day behind the wheel. what does a Sikh retire into?

segments.voice: Yesterday, wealth without pride: gift, not ranking. The Giver keeps giving. Today the question is what happens when the giving seems to stop.
screen: `GIFT, NOT RANKING.` → `WHEN THE GIVING SEEMS TO STOP.`

segments.voice: The email arrives on a Tuesday at ten: a meeting invite, fifteen minutes, with someone from HR. Aman, who marries Simran's cousin Jasleen on Saturday, is out of a job by lunch. That night the family sits in Bebe's kitchen, and two good people say two different things. Bebe, quietly: this is the Guru's will, beta, take it sweetly. Harjit, already on his phone: it's a setback, so we work, and we start tonight. Simran looks from one to the other. They can't both be right. Can they?
screen: `A FIFTEEN-MINUTE MEETING.` → `BEBE: TAKE IT SWEETLY.` → `HARJIT: WE START TONIGHT.`

segments.voice: Let each of them speak. Bebe's side has deep roots. The Japji opens by saying the way through is to walk in the hukam, the order of the One. And on ang 394, Guru Arjan says, in paraphrase, whatever You do seems sweet to me. Her best case: when you fight what has already happened, you suffer twice, and acceptance frees your strength for what comes next. Harjit's side has roots too. On ang 522, Guru Arjan says, in paraphrase, keep making the effort and live; earn, and enjoy peace. Sikhi praises kirat, honest work, and the sangat, the community, is meant to carry its own. His best case: acceptance can slide into giving up, and a family waiting quietly for a sign may miss a job a friend could find by Friday. Both of them hold one thing in common, and it has a name. Chardi kala: rising spirits, the high mood Sikhs pray for at the close of Ardas. Some Sikhs hear both voices in that line: accept the will, and keep the spirit climbing. By midnight Bebe has packed Aman a tiffin of parathas, and Harjit has texted four drivers who know four other companies.
screen: `BEBE: WALK IN THE HUKAM.` · `ANG 394: YOUR WILL IS SWEET.` · `HARJIT: ANG 522, MAKE THE EFFORT.` · `CHARDI KALA: RISING SPIRITS.` · then, large: `RISE ANYWAY.`

segments.voice: Sit up slowly, as if a thread were lifting the crown of your head, and let your shoulders drop away from your ears. Rest your hands palms up on your knees. Stay tall and easy like that for the sit, risen, without any strain.
Losing work. A blow the Sikh tradition meets with chardi kala, and with the sangat's help.
Rise anyway, with the will accepted and the spirit still climbing, and a few friends texting leads. Until tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 1669 COUNTS.` → `LIVING IT · 43 OF 134.` → `TOMORROW: WHAT DOES A SIKH RETIRE INTO?`

howItsDone: When someone in the sangat loses work, Sikhs may offer Ardas for them at the gurdwara, and friends often pass on job leads and help practically.

match.prompt: two voices in one kitchen — tap the pairs.
pairs: walk in the hukam; take it sweetly
rising spirits, prayed for in Ardas

myth: accepting God's will in Sikhi means sitting still and waiting
ang 522 praises effort, and the sangat is meant to carry its own.
chardi kala is prayed for at the close of Ardas
rising spirits: the high mood Sikhs ask for, even in loss.
the sangat's job ends at the gurdwara door
Harjit's texts to drivers are the sangat at work.

fork.setup: a friend who lost her job says, 'it's God's will, so i'll just wait.' you lean toward Harjit. state Bebe's side at its best first.
options: fighting what's happened makes you suffer twice; acceptance frees strength for what's next.
acceptance is just a nicer word for being too scared to try.
waiting is right because effort makes no difference to the will.
fork.reveal: a fair debate starts with the other side's best case. Bebe's is that acceptance frees you; Harjit's is that effort keeps acceptance from becoming giving up.

original.note: Gurmukhi: chardi kala, rising spirits, prayed for at the close of Ardas.

trapdoor: what you thought: losing a job is either fate to accept or a fight to win.
what it means: rise anyway: accept what's happened, keep the spirit climbing, and let the sangat help.
what a scholar hears: hukam in the Japji's first pauri, ang 394's 'Your doing seems sweet', ang 522's call to effort, and chardi kala at Ardas's close.
guess: a job loss met with rising spirits and community help
a sign that a family has fallen out of God's favor
a time to step away from the sangat until you recover
recall: ask who gets it, then give

chat.says: aman keeps saying it's fine, it's god's will. but he hasn't applied anywhere. do i say something
options: accepting it is good. maybe ask if he wants help sending a few out.
leave it. if it's god's will, effort won't change anything anyway.
tell him accepting is weak and he needs to stop praying and hustle.
chat.meaning: Bebe's acceptance and Harjit's effort both have roots in the Granth; chardi kala holds them together, and the sangat helps.

hukam.meaning: the order or will of the One

Chardi kala.meaning: rising spirits; a high, hopeful mood

Ardas.meaning: the standing prayer said at Sikh gatherings

tiffin.meaning: a packed lunch, often in a stacked steel box
